title: Installing SQL Server and Management Tools
description: Step through installing SQL Server (Developer Edition) and SQL Server Management Studio on Windows, plus a quick intro to Azure Data Studio.

data.text: Before you can write your first query, you need a running SQL Server instance and a tool to talk to it. This lesson walks through the two installers you need and how to confirm everything is working.

items: A Windows PC (10 or 11) or Windows Server — SQL Server runs natively on Windows
At least 6 GB of free disk space (Express is smaller)
An active internet connection for the download

data.title: Using macOS or Linux?
data.text: SQL Server is available on Linux, but the simplest path for beginners is Windows + SSMS. If you are on a Mac, you can use Azure Data Studio (cross-platform) to connect to a SQL Server running on a cloud VM or Docker container.
Step 1 — Install the SQL Server database engine

data.title: Download and run the installer
data.content:
1. Go to the Microsoft SQL Server Downloads page and select the Developer edition.
2. Run the installer (EXE) and choose 'Basic' installation.
3. When prompted, select Mixed Mode authentication and set a strong 'sa' password.
4. Complete the wizard and restart if prompted.

data.title: Remember your 'sa' password
data.text: During setup, write down the password you set for the built-in 'sa' (system administrator) account. You will need it to log in — and if you forget it, recovering is painful.
Step 2 — Install SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)

data.title: Installing SSMS
data.content:
1. Download the SSMS installer from Microsoft's website.
2. Run it — it is a small bootstrapper that downloads the rest automatically.
3. Once installed, launch SSMS and sign in with the SQL Server instance you just configured.

data.text: SSMS is a heavy, Windows-only application with a full graphical interface. For a lighter, cross-platform experience, download Azure Data Studio instead — it supports Windows, macOS, and Linux, and uses 'extensions' for extra features.
When you open SSMS, the 'Connect to Server' dialog asks for a server name. If you installed SQL Server with the default options, the server name is:

data.title: Connection details
data.content:
Server name:  localhost
Authentication:  SQL Server Authentication
Login:  sa
Password:  [the password you set during setup]

data.title: What 'localhost' means
data.text: 'localhost' tells SSMS to connect to a SQL Server instance running on your own computer. If you see your computer name (e.g., 'MYPC') instead, that works too.

data.title: Hello, SQL Server!
data.content:
-- The simplest possible T-SQL query
SELECT 1 + 1 AS Result;

data.text: In SSMS, open a 'New Query' window, paste that code, and click the 'Execute' button (or press F5). If you see a result of 2, your setup is working.

data.title: Installation checklist
points: Install SQL Server Developer Edition with Mixed Mode authentication
Install SSMS or Azure Data Studio on your development machine
Connect using 'localhost' as the server name and the 'sa' account
Run 'SELECT 1 + 1 AS Result' to confirm the connection works
